$comment: GENERATED by scripts/generate-rush-wave-models.mjs from data/rush-cards.json. The Rush's wave-model demand templates (DECISIONS.md section D1636), in data/traffic-profiles.json's demandTemplates record shape. They are kept out of that file on purpose: it is part of every run's configuration and of the inputs pinned measurements are hashed over, and a rush round is the only run that reads these.

templates.name: Rush: Surges
templates.shape: the climb in surges: every three-minute wave is a lull and then a crest, each wave bigger than the last
templates.$comment: GENERATED by scripts/generate-rush-wave-models.mjs from data/rush-cards.json and never edited by hand. A Rush wave model (DECISIONS.md section D1636): the endless-rush climb, wave for wave, with a different rhythm inside each three-minute wave. Intensity is against this model's own peak, peakFactor x wave 30's rate, which packages/core/src/sim/rushCards.ts converts to the run's arrival rate. NOT CITED and a demonstration on the footing endless-rush states (section D478): the rate leaves every declared band on purpose. DERIVED: each stretch holds its rate and ramps to the next over its last 30 s, because rule 6 of config/demandPhases.ts admits no step, which is the compromise endless-rush states. CLOCK, NOT CITED: 08:00 is a placement, the hour endless-rush opens at, so every card opens where the climb does. selectable is false, so no list offers it and no judged surface names it (docs/35 PM-RU2).

templates.name: Rush: Tides
templates.shape: the climb with the tide turning: half of every wave pours in at the lobby and half pours out of the floors, each wave bigger than the last
